eyebrow: How a scanner spots a secret

steps.label: Regex pattern matching
steps.sub: known shapes — AKIA..., ghp_..., xoxb- — fast but blind to the unknown

steps.label: Shannon entropy scoring
steps.sub: flags strings too random to be normal code, catches secrets with no known format

steps.label: Real tools run both
steps.sub: gitleaks, detect-secrets, and trufflehog combine the two, tunable per repo

code:
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
    rev: v8.18.4
    hooks:
      - id: gitleaks

# pip install pre-commit
# pre-commit install
caption: Runs on every `git commit` — but only on a machine where it was actually installed.

eyebrow: Deleting a file doesn't delete history
code:
# scan every commit on every branch and tag
gitleaks detect --source . --log-opts="--all" \
  --report-path gitleaks-report.json

# confirm which findings are live, exploitable secrets
trufflehog git file://. --only-verified
caption: A secret removed in a later commit is still sitting in the earlier one.

eyebrow: A real leak happened — now what

steps.label: 1. Rotate the credential at its source
steps.sub: the only step that stops the leaked copy from being usable

steps.label: 2. Audit access logs for the exposure window
steps.sub: find out whether this was a close call or an active compromise
